name: Badging API
plain: Shows a number or dot on the app icon.
meaning: Alerts the person to unread items without a notification. Cannot read badge state.

access.prompt_ui: None; needs installed app and sometimes notification permission
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

chrome.note: Windows and macOS since Chrome 81. ChromeOS since Chrome 91. Linux offers no universal badging API on the operating system level.

edge.note: Windows and macOS since Edge 81. ChromeOS since Edge 91. Linux offers no universal badging API on the operating system level.

safari.note: Badging is supported for installed web apps on macOS Sonoma and higher. Passing 0 as an argument will clear the badge instead of displaying an unnu

ios_safari.note: Badging is supported for web apps saved to the home screen. Passing 0 as an argument will clear the badge instead of displaying an unnumbered dot.

data.metric: Shows a number or dot on the app icon.

fields.name: count
fields.precision: icon shows digits up to OS limit

limits.headline: Can show a number or dot on an installed app's icon, but can't check it
limits.user_action: You install the web app and, on iPhone, allow notifications
can: Show an unread count or dot on the app icon
Update it when something new arrives
Clear it once you open the item
cannot: Work for a site that is not installed as an app
Check what number is already showing
Work on iPhone without notification permission
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Safari support it for installed apps. iPhone also needs notification permission. Firefox does not.

story.what_it_is: An installed web app can show a number or dot on its app icon.

marketing.name: Badging API
marketing.pitch: Installed web apps can show a badge on the icon to say there is something new.

story.for_you: You see a small number or dot on the app icon in the dock or taskbar. It tells you there are new items. There is no pop up to dismiss.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to draw you back. A count on the icon is a low cost nudge that works with push messages. It only works for installed web apps.

use_cases.example: A chat web app installed on your PC shows how many unread chats you have.
A web mail app shows a count of unread mail on its icon.
A browser game shows a dot when a turn or reward is waiting.
A social web app shows the number of new replies.
A store app shows a dot when a deal or order update arrives.
A task app shows how many tasks are due.
A news app shows unread top stories.
